question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct Lesson 8 retrieval, exact definitions, familiar-pair classification, direction-based comparison, completeness diagnosis, a multi-record classification and property explanation, then a mixed earlier-module reporting audit with current scalar-vector reasoning

evidence_basis.originality_note: All wording, record sets and figure briefs are newly authored. The eight mapped P2 leaves and their seven complete source-question contexts ground exact definitions, classification, valid examples and the need for direction. Their later-topic calculations and diagrams are excluded.

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, a measured length is recorded as (15.0 ± 0.6) cm. Calculate its percentage uncertainty.
State what is meant by a scalar quantity and by a vector quantity.
Which pair contains two vector quantities?
An object reverses its direction of motion while the numerical magnitude shown on a meter stays the same. Which statement correctly compares a scalar reading with a vector reading?

options.A: A scalar and a vector must both have changed.
options.B: A scalar is unchanged, but a vector has changed.
options.C: A vector is unchanged, but a scalar has changed.
options.D: Neither type can be affected by direction.

questions.prompt: Which record is incomplete because a required direction is missing?
A monitoring panel reports six physical quantities for a small research vehicle: time, speed, energy, acceleration, force and momentum.

figure.purpose: Present a compact mixed set of familiar quantities for classification and comparison without revealing the categories
figure.brief: Create an original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular line diagram of a simple vehicle monitoring panel. Show six separate labelled readouts: time 18 s, speed 12 m s^-1, energy 2.0 kJ, acceleration 0.60 m s^-2 south, force 40 N downward and momentum 4.8 kg m s^-1 north. Do not group, colour-code, tick or label any readout as scalar or vector.
figure.alt_text: A vehicle monitoring panel lists time, speed, energy, acceleration, force and momentum with their recorded values.
